title: Third-Party Application Patching with Intune
author_notes: Effort tier: T3 (multi-component within Intune: Enterprise App Catalog + Win32 update packaging, detection, supersedence, ring assignment for non-Microsoft apps).
hook: Patch the apps attackers actually target — Chrome, Adobe, Zoom and more — automatically, from Intune
problem: Windows Update keeps the OS current, but the software that gets exploited most — browsers, Adobe Reader, Java, Zoom, 7-Zip, and dozens of other third-party apps — quietly drifts out of date on every device. Each unpatched version is an open door. This solution gives you a repeatable third-party patching program in Intune: use the Enterprise App Catalog where available and a packaged update method elsewhere, with detection and supersedence so devices move to the current version automatically, deployed in rings.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — why third-party apps are the prime attack surface, the Enterprise App Catalog (catalog apps with auto-update) model, the packaged/superseded Win32 update method for everything else, and the ring-based update model.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, app inventory, Enterprise App Catalog availability, packaging tooling for non-catalog apps, detection method, maintenance windows) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: inventory installed third-party apps and versions, onboard catalog apps with auto-update, package and supersede non-catalog apps, set detection and assignment rings, schedule updates, then validate and expand.

5 PowerShell scripts — installed third-party app/version discovery, patch-state validation, an out-of-date exposure report across the fleet, safe remediation of stuck updates, and an update-ring group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: A repeatable third-party patching program in Intune for the apps attackers target most — Chrome, Adobe, Zoom and more — via the Enterprise App Catalog and packaged updates with detection, supersedence, and rings. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
short_plain: A repeatable third-party patching program in Intune for non-Microsoft apps — Enterprise App Catalog plus packaged updates, with detection, supersedence, and rings.
meta_description: Patch non-Microsoft apps with Intune: Enterprise App Catalog auto-update, packaged Win32 update method, detection, supersedence, and ring-based deployment. Self-guided, tested steps and scripts.
bottom_line: Your highest-risk third-party apps kept current automatically across the fleet — catalog apps auto-updating, everything else packaged and superseded, deployed in rings — proven on a pilot before you scale.
